newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bardot rapped for alleged racist slur on Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Bardot rapped for alleged racist slur on Moslems.

text.p: A French anti-racism association said on Tuesday it planned to take former screen goddess Brigitte Bardot to court after she launched a new attack on the Aid-el-Kebir Moslem feast and its slaughtering of sheep.
The Movement Against Racism (MRAP) group accused Bardot in a statement of "hiding behind freedom of expression to pass on xenophobic, vulgar and dangerous messages".

Bardot, who heads a foundation protecting animal rights, had written in a statement published earlier on Tuesday: "People are slitting the throats of women and children, our monks, our officials, our tourists and our sheep."
Her statement was a reference to French monks killed by alleged Moslem fundamentalists in Algeria and to other victims of violence in the North African country.
"Once again, Aid-al-Kebir will bloody the land of France, on April 17, with the blood of sheep whose throats have been slit, all too often anywhere and any old how or clandestinely," she said.
MRAP, which last year unsuccessfully sued Bardot for inciting racial hatred, accused her of making no difference between Moslems and fundamentalists.
A Paris court in January cleared Bardot of MRAP's previous charges after she said France was being invaded by sheep-slaughtering Moslems.
The court said her comments were "above all the expression of rebellion against animal distress made as part of a passionate struggle for animal rights".
